findings.claim: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is a no-op/dead write: with empty data Prisma 5.4.2 does not bump @updatedAt, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt), and it adds an extra UPDATE round-trip on every webhook/cron fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run. The new repository method at packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400 exists only for this caller.
findings.evidence: Line 1024 passes {}; grep finds updateManyByCredentialId only at its definition (selectedCalendar.ts:400) and this caller; no consumer of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt in the patch. Prisma empty-data behaviour reasoned, not run against a DB.
findings.reason: Three of the four seats rated this Important (the fourth Minor), and the grep for a consumer supports it. Remove the call and the repository method. Red check: an integration test asserting SelectedCalendar.updatedAt changes after fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, which needs a database.

findings.claim: sed -i '' -E is BSD/macOS-only syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) the .env update fails with exit 2 but the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated. The script is also unrelated to the cache feature (scope creep).
findings.evidence: Reproduced by two seats: printf 'GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=old\n' > t.env && sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=new|" t.env -> "sed: can't read s|...: No such file or directory", rc=2, file unchanged.
findings.reason: Reproduced on GNU sed. The fix is a portable in-place edit, or dropping the script from this PR.

findings.claim: ENV_FILE="../.env" depends on the caller's working directory. The cleanup function exits 0 on failure paths, and when an existing tmole process is reused it reads a possibly stale or missing /tmp/tmole.log.
findings.evidence: Line 5 hard-codes a relative path; per OCR, cleanup at lines 17/49/58 exits 0.
findings.reason: Cheap correctness fixes in the same file as the accepted sed finding, or moot if the script is dropped.

findings.claim: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select in findUnlockedUserForSession (every session lookup), and the UserWithCalendars Pick type in packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28 is widened to require them, but nothing reads either field.
findings.evidence: A grep for googleChannelId/.updatedAt across the calendars router, the selected-calendars atoms and CredentialActionsDropdown hits only the type lines. Breaches .cursor/rules/review.mdc 'Only select data you need'.
findings.reason: Breaks a documented repo standard; reverting both hunks is trivial.

findings.claim: new CalendarCacheRepository() is constructed directly, bypassing CalendarCache.init's feature-flag gate (calendar-cache.ts:24-28). Cache status and the 'Delete cached data' action therefore show even when calendar-cache is off, and the getCacheStatusByCredentialIds additions to calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts and calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts are unreachable.
findings.evidence: Line 28 instantiates the concrete repository; the factory that returns the mock when the flag is off is never called on this path.
findings.reason: A real behaviour gap (the UI ignores the feature flag) and dead mock code. Respect the flag, or drop the interface and mock edits.

findings.claim: After the deleteCache mutation succeeds it only calls onSuccess?.(); it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. Callers that pass no onChanged (e.g. EventAdvancedTab) keep showing the stale 'Last updated' timestamp after a delete. The disconnect mutation in the same file does invalidate in onSettled.
findings.evidence: Lines 43-45: the onSuccess body has no utils invalidate call, unlike the disconnect mutation's onSettled.
findings.reason: Reasoned stale-UI bug with a one-line fix.

findings.claim: hasCache ignores disableConnectionModification, so the event-type Advanced tab (EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372 passes disableConnectionModification={true}), which previously showed no credential actions, now shows a destructive 'Delete cached data' item.
findings.evidence: Line 69: hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt has no modification gate; rendering at lines 71/82 depends only on canDisconnect and hasCache.
findings.reason: Whether deleting the cache counts as 'connection modification' is a product decision. ponytail: confirm intent with the feature owner before gating.

findings.claim: The cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...), ignoring the user's locale and profile timezone, even though the label beside it uses t().
findings.evidence: Line 89 literal "en-US"; .cursor/rules/review.mdc requires localisation in frontend code.
findings.reason: Cheap fix: use the locale from useLocale.

findings.claim: The read-only cache-status block is a focusable, selectable DropdownMenuItem that does nothing, and it uses raw text-gray-900/text-gray-500/dark:text-white instead of the design-system tokens (text-emphasis, text-subtle).
findings.evidence: Lines 86-87 raw gray classes; the status block is wrapped in a menu item with no action.
findings.reason: Low-cost consistency and accessibility fix.

findings.claim: Imports @calcom/platform-constants, which packages/features/package.json does not declare. This is the first such import in packages/features; it resolves only through workspace hoisting.
findings.evidence: Line 6 import; the @calcom deps in packages/features/package.json are atoms, dayjs, lib, trpc and ui.
findings.reason: Undeclared dependency; declare it, or import the constant from a declared package.

findings.claim: The disconnect mutation, toasts, invalidations and confirm dialog are copied from DisconnectIntegration.tsx instead of reusing it, and the copy drops the original's teamId passthrough and isDelegationCredential({credentialId}) guard.
findings.evidence: Compare DisconnectIntegration.tsx:26-46 with CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:53-65 and 143-154.
findings.reason: Reuse the existing component rather than keep two copies that have already drifted.

findings.claim: The component takes six props, four only to derive canDisconnect/hasCache, and the same six-prop block is duplicated at two call sites in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx (70-79, 123-132).
findings.evidence: Cites .cursor/rules/review.mdc 'Prefer Composition over Prop Drilling'; the seat itself called it a judgement call.
findings.reason: Advisory judgement call with no defect. ponytail: revisit if the dropdown gains more actions.

findings.claim: A failed ownership check throws a plain Error, so the client gets INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.
findings.evidence: Line 25 throw new Error(...); the sibling setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts imports and throws TRPCError with codes.
findings.reason: All seats agree; one-line fix to TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" }).

findings.claim: prisma.credential.findFirst has no select, so it loads the full Credential row, including key (OAuth tokens), only for an existence/ownership check.
findings.evidence: Line 17 findFirst without select; .cursor/rules/review.mdc: 'Only select data you need' and names app credentials. The key is not returned to the client.
findings.reason: Documented-standard breach on the credentials table; select: { id: true } suffices. Normalised from Important (MP, advisory) to Minor because nothing is exposed.

findings.claim: The cache delete calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly from the tRPC handler, while the cache-status read goes through CalendarCacheRepository; the layering is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Line 28 vs connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28; no documented rule mandates repositories.
findings.reason: Heuristic only; no documented standard is breached. ponytail: move into CalendarCacheRepository when that file is next touched.

findings.claim: The deleteCache input schema is inlined with z.object instead of a deleteCache.schema.ts, and the procedure is missing from CalendarsRouterHandlerCache, which breaks this router's convention.
findings.evidence: Sibling procedures use ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema/ZSetDestinationCalendarInputSchema from *.schema.ts files (lines 1-11).
findings.reason: Cheap alignment with the local convention.

findings.claim: No tests were added for the new code: deleteCacheHandler (including its ownership check), getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, the cacheUpdatedAt field in connectedCalendars, and the dropdown UI.
findings.evidence: The router already has handler tests (e.g. setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts); the patch adds none.
findings.reason: The ownership check guards a destructive mutation and needs a test.

findings.claim: Undocumented behaviour change: in the error/Alert branch, 'Remove app' used to be hidden only for delegation credentials and is now also hidden when disableConnectionModification is set, so users there can no longer remove a broken credential.
findings.evidence: The removed lines gated only on !connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId; the new component also gates on !disableConnectionModification.
findings.reason: Arguably more consistent with the flag's meaning; needs a product decision. ponytail: confirm whether broken credentials must stay removable when modification is disabled.

findings.claim: Unrelated churn: delegationCredentialId={... || null} and a lone blank line at 162.
findings.evidence: Lines 98 and 162 of the diff.
findings.reason: Harmless: || null only normalises undefined to null for the prop and changes no behaviour. Not a defect.

findings.claim: An unrelated refactor of findMany removes the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` type check.
findings.evidence: The hunk replaces `const args = {...} satisfies ...; findMany(args)` with `findMany({ where, select, orderBy })`.
findings.reason: No loss of type safety: the object is now passed inline to prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany, whose parameter type checks it (selectedCalendar.ts:260). Two seats (SP, OCR) also found no behaviour change.

findings.claim: dev:cron switches from ts-node (still declared at line 196) to `npx tsx`. tsx is not declared or in yarn.lock, so npx downloads it at run time, and the change is unrelated to the feature.
findings.evidence: The tsx grep across the package.json files finds no dependency; ts-node is still declared.
findings.reason: Undeclared runtime download plus scope creep; revert or declare tsx.

findings.claim: The auto-generated warning header says the required column is added 'without a default value', but the SQL adds DEFAULT NOW(), so the comment is stale and misleading.
findings.evidence: Lines 1-6 header vs line 9 DEFAULT NOW().
findings.reason: Delete the stale header. PT's extra point, that the explanatory comments breach a 'no comments' rule, is rejected: that rule is the user's global preference, not a documented repo standard.

findings.claim: DEFAULT NOW() backfills existing CalendarCache rows with the migration time, so 'Last updated' is wrong for them until their next refresh.
findings.evidence: The migration adds updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW(); there is no backfill from any existing column.
findings.reason: Cosmetic and self-healing (@updatedAt bumps on the next upsert). ponytail: acceptable unless an accurate pre-migration timestamp matters.

findings.claim: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds takes the max updatedAt without filtering expired rows (expiresAt), so a status can show for a fully expired cache.
findings.evidence: The groupBy where clause contains only credentialId.
findings.reason: 'Last updated' is still factually correct for expired rows; whether to hide expired caches is a product call. ponytail: filter on expiresAt if the status is meant to mean 'cache active'.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): no dependency install, typecheck, lint, build or tests. No spec, so the spec-compliance axis was limited to scope notes. Documented standards found: .cursor/rules/review.mdc, CONTRIBUTING.md, packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md; the repo has no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. All 4 seats reviewed all 17 files in the patch; apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json was only checked for key usage (ponytail). The untracked harness dotfiles in the worktree (.bashrc, .claude/, .mcp.json, etc.) were excluded from the pinned patch as not part of the PR. Unverified claims: the Prisma empty-data updateMany behaviour (needs a DB). Stopped after the merge per benchmark overrides: no fixes, red tests or round 2+.
